questions.question: The honour of Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship carries ______________.

options.text: Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram
Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship:**

__
 
• It is also known as **Akademi Ratna Sadasyata**.
 
• **The greatest award bestowed by Sangeet Natak Akademi, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, caste, religion, creed, or sex, is the Fellowship.**
 
• Anybody under 50 is not ordinarily eligible to be considered for the honor according to the criteria.
 
• The members of the Akademi General Council as well as the existing fellows provide recommendations.
 
• Up until 2008, only 30 distinguished individuals could receive the most coveted and rare Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna Sadasyata) at any given time. 
 
• However, ten (10) additional Akademi Fellow seats have been added as a result of the Rules and Regulations being amended at the General Council meeting on January 29, 2010, with two seats being filled each year. This expansion will take place gradually over the course of five years.
 
• The **Akademi elected its first Fellow in 1954.**
 
• To date, it has named 153 notable individuals as Akademi Fellows (Akademi Ratna).
 
• **The Akademi Fellowship includes an Angavastram, a Tamrapatra, and purse money totaling Rs. 3.00 lakhs. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship awardee in 2018**:

 
• Zakir Hussain
 
• Jatin Goswami
 
• Sonal Mansingh
 
• Thiruvidaimarudur Kuppiah Kalyanasundram

**Sangeet Natak Akademi**:

 
• India's premier performing arts organization, Sangeet Natak Akademi, was** founded in 1953.**
 
• With the goal of preserving and advancing the rich intangible cultural legacy of the nation, which is reflected in its many musical, dance, and theatrical traditions.
 
• The General Council of the Akademi is in charge of overseeing it.
 
• The** President of India appoints the Chairman** **of the Akademi to a five-year term.**
 
• The Indian government's Ministry of Culture oversees Sangeet Natak Akademi as an autonomous entity. 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi has bestowed following awards:**
 
 
• Sangeet Natak Academy Fellowship (Ratna Sadashya)
 
• Sangeet Natak Academy Award (Akademi Puraskar)
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar (**Instituted in 2006**)

questions.question: Mawsynram in the ______ of the Khasi Hills receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Southern**__** part.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mawsynram:**

 
 
• Mawsynram is a town located 69 kilometers from Shillong, the state capital of Meghalaya state in northeastern India, in the Southern Khasi Hills area.
 
• In India, Mawsynram experiences the most rainfall.
 
• It is said to be the wettest site on Earth, receiving** 11,872 millimeters of rain **on average per year.
 
• The **Guinness Book of World Records states that Mawsynram saw 26,000 millimeters of rain in 1985.**
 
• Mawsynram is a popular tourist destination known for its scenic beauty, waterfalls, and limestone caves.
 
• Traveling to Phlangwanbroi village enables nature enthusiasts to go deep into the jungle, which is home to colonies of protected Hoolock Gibbons.
 
• Worldwide, **Krem Puri is the world's longest sandstone cave.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Tribe:**

 
 
• **An ethnic group in northeastern India's Meghalaya state is known as the Khasi people.**
 
• **Khasi Hills** are home to the Khasi people
 
• They are one of the few South Asian populations **speaking Austronasiatic**.
 
• One of the few tribes in the world that still practice matriarchy is the Khasi tribe.
 
• Khasi region is also known for its tea and orange plantations.
 
 
 
• **There are three possible causes for Mawsynram's heavy rainfall:**
 
 
• During the monsoon, warm, humid winds from the Bay of Bengal push northward, covering a large area before being forced to converge into a tighter zone over the Khasi Hills, where they concentrate their moisture.
 
• The Khasi Hills' east-west alignment puts them squarely in the line of the Bay of Bengal breeze, which causes a considerable uplift as well as cooling, additional condensation, and consequently more rain.
 
• Lastly, during the monsoon season, uplift over the Khasi Hills is almost continual due to strong winds in the upper atmosphere continuously drawing the lifted air upward, which results in nearly constant rainfall.

questions.question: ________________, established in 1829, is the oldest golf club in India and the first outside Great Britain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Royal Calcutta Golf Club.**__

__
 
• **The Royal Calcutta Golf Club was established in 1829, making it the oldest golf club in India.**
 
• **It is also the first golf club established outside of Great Britain.**
 
• The club is located **in Kolkata** and has a rich history, having hosted several prestigious golf tournaments.
 
• **Some of the notable members of the club include famous Indian cricketer Sourav Ganguly and former Indian President Pranab Mukherjee.**

** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The Legislative Council of a state assembly __________ of the total number of members in the legislative of the state and in no case fewer than 40 members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's legislature is divided into two houses.
 
• **Article 169 of the Constitution allows the states to have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in addition to the Legislative Assembly ( Vidhan Sabha), much as Parliament has two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).**
 
• Article 169 (Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States): Parliament may by law provide for the abolition of the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council or for the creation of such a Council in a State having no such Council, if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by a majority of not less than 2/3rd of the members of the Assembly present and voting.
 
• **A state's Legislative Council may not have fewer than 40 members or more than one-third of the State Assembly's total membership, as stated in Article 171 of the Constitution.**
 
• At present, 6 States have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
 
• The tenure of a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) is 6 years, with 1/3rd of the members retiring every two years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Manner of Election of Members of the Legislative Council (MLC)**: **Article 171**

 
• **The state's MLAs elect 1/3rd of the MLCs.**
 
• **An additional 1/3rd will be chosen by a special electorate made up of current district board and municipality members.**
 
• 1/12th are chosen by registered graduates of at least three years standing and 1/12th by teachers of secondary schools having at least three years experience.
 
• **The governor appoints the remaining members (about 1/6th) in recognition of their remarkable contributions to the cooperative movement, literature, science, art, and social service, among other fields.**

questions.question: Mahavir Jayanti is celebrated in the month of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**March-April.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahavir Jayanti:**

 
 
• For the **Jain community**, Mahavir Jayanti is one of the most auspicious holidays.
 
• **The 24th and final Tirthankara (enlightened teacher) Mahavir of the Jain religion is born on this day.**
 
• Achieving global peace and harmony in a way that harms living things as little as possible is highly valued in Jainism.
 
• Jains across celebrate Mahavir Jayanti with great enthusiasm.
 
• **On this auspicious day, they recite songs in praise of Lord Mahavirs, meditate, visit temples, go on processions (rath yatra), and pay alms to the needy. **
 
 
 
• **Vardhman Mahavir:**
 
 
• In the former Vaishali kingdom, **King Siddhartha and Queen Trishala gave birth to Lord Mahavira. **
 
• The precise date of Mahvira's birth is a topic of discussion among Jains.
 
• **The Swetambar Jains date his birth to 599 BC, whereas the Degambar Jains place his birth year at 615 BC.**
 
• The 13th day of the month of Chaitra is when Lord Mahavira was born, according to the Hindu calendar.
 
• At thirty years old, Mahavira gave up all of his material belongings and set out to become a nomadic ascetic in pursuit of enlightenment.
 
• According to tradition, after going into exile for 12 years, he achieved "Kevala Jnana," or omniscience.
 
• The teachings of non-violence, honesty, non-stealing, chastity, and non-attachment were the focus of Lord Mahavira's life.
 
• He advocated treating all living things with love, compassion, and respect since they all have souls.
 
• He also emphasized the value of leading a straightforward, tranquil, and moral life.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Some other festivals of Jains:**

 
 
• **Paryushana:**

 
 
• **The most significant yearly religious occasion for Jains is Das Lakshana, also known as Paryushana, which is often observed in August or September during the Bhadrapad Month's Shukla Paksha in the Hindi calendar.**
 
• Jains frequently use prayer, meditation, and fasting to heighten their spiritual intensity.
 
• This is the time to highlight the five primary vowels.
 
• Followers are encouraged to practice in accordance with their aptitude and desires, and there are no established regulations.
 
• Śvētāmbaras refer to it as Paryushana ("abiding" or "coming together"), whereas Digambaras refer to it as Das Lakshana Dharma.
 
• For Śvētāmbara Jains, Paryushana lasts for eight days, whereas for Jains of the Digambara sect, it lasts for ten days.
 
• **The celebration of Samvatsari, also known as Kshamavani (forgiveness day), marks the completion of the festival.**
 
 
 
• **Samvatsari:**
 
 
• **Saṃvatsari, also known as Annual Day or Forgiveness Day, falls on the last day of the Paryushana Shvetambara Jaina sect.**
 
• **Every year, in the Jain month of Bhadrapada, it falls on Shukla Choth; on the Gregorian calendar, it falls between mid-August and mid-September.**
 
• On this day, Jains ask for and accept forgiveness from all living things for whatever mistakes they may have made, whether they were intentional or not.
 
• On this day every year, an intricate penitential retreat known as "samvatsari pratikramana" is conducted.
 
• Following the pratikramana, Jains repeat Micchami Dukkadam, or variations such as "Khamau Sa," "Uttam Kshama," or "Khamat Khamna" in order to ask for forgiveness from all living things, including friends and family.

questions.question: __________banks are owned by their customers and follow the cooperative principle of one person, one vote.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooperative.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cooperative Banks:**

 
 
• **It is a cooperatively organized institution designed to handle standard banking operations.**
 
• **The founding principles of cooperative banks are share collections, deposit acceptance, and loan disbursements.**
 
• These are cooperative credit societies, where community members band together to lend money to one another on advantageous terms.
 
• They adhere to the cooperative principle of one member, one vote, which guarantees each participant an equal voice in the process of making decisions.
 
• **They are registered under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, or the Cooperative Societies Act of the relevant State.**
 
• The **Co-operative banks are governed by:**
 
 
• Banking Regulations Act, 1949
 
• Banking Laws (Co-operative Societies) Act, 1955
 
 
 
• **They can be generically categorized as**:
 
 
• Urban cooperative banks
 
• Rural cooperative banks
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Bank:**

 
 
• **Scheduled banks are those that fall under Schedule II of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.**
 
• **To be classified as a scheduled bank, the bank's raised capital and paid-up capital must total at least Rs. 5 lakh. **
 
• The RBI may provide these banks with low interest loans.
 
• They are clearing house members as well.
 
• They also have a lot of responsibilities to meet, like keeping the central bank's average daily cash reserve ratio.
 
 
 
• **Nationalised Bank:**
 
 
• These are **also known as Public Sector Bank.**
 
• **Banks classified as public sector in which the public interest is the primary goal and the government has retained a majority of its share.**
 
• In order to enter the banking industry after gaining independence, the Indian government began nationalising the Imperial Bank of India in 1955.
 
• It was renamed as The State Bank of India after the Reserve Bank of India acquired 60% of the company.
 
• The** Indian government nationalized fourteen more banks in 1969.**

questions.question: Which of the following state hosted the Khelo India Youth Games 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Haryana__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The fourth edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2021 was hosted in Panchkula, Haryana.**

 
 
• After being postponed three times due to COVID-19, it was held from 4–13 June 2022​
 
• It was held in five different cities: Panchkula, Shahabad, Ambala, Chandigarh and Delhi. 
 
 
 
• Some 4,700 athletes, including 2,262 women, from all of India’s 36 states and Union Territories participated at KIYG 2021.
 
• A total of 903 medals across 25 different sports were awarded at KIYG 2021.
 
• **Five indigenous sports, mallakhamb, gatka, kalaripayattu, thang-ta and yogasana, also made their KIYG debut.**
 
• Hosts Haryana won the KIYG 2021 with 52 gold medals, followed by Maharashtra with 45 and Karnataka with 22.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **The Khelo India initiative**, which translates to ‘Let’s play India’, was proposed by the government of India **in 2017** to revive India’s sporting culture by engaging with children at the grassroots level.

 
 
• Under this movement, the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), the Khelo India University Games (KIUG) and the Khelo India Winter Games were set up as annual national sports competitions where youngsters, representing their states and universities, respectively, showcased their skills and competed for medals.
 
 
 
• **The Khelo India Youth Games is an annual national sports event for athletes under-17 and under-21 years of age.**
 
• **The 1st edition was held in Delhi in 2018.**
 
• Maharashtra hosted the 2nd edition of the Khelo India Youth Games in 2019, which was held in Pune.
 
 
• Haryana topped the medals table in the inaugural edition in 2018, then called the Khelo India School Games, but Maharashtra beat them down to second in 2019 and 2020.

questions.question: What is conversion of oil to vanaspati termed as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogenation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**Hydrogenation of Oil:**

 
• As vegetable oils have long chains and double bonds, they can go through addition processes. These substances are unsaturated. Vegetable ghee, also referred to as vanaspati ghee, is created by heating vegetable oils in the presence of Nickel catalyst, which changes the unsaturated fat into saturated fat.
 
• This process is called the hydrogenation of oil

questions.question: Solid Carbon dioxide is commonly called as ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dry ice.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

 
• Solid carbon dioxide (CO₂) is commonly known as dry ice because it does not melt like regular ice but instead sublimates directly from a solid into a gas.
 
• It is colorless, odorless, and non-flammable and can lower the pH of a solution when dissolved in water, forming carbonic acid (H₂CO₃)
 
• **It is used for various purposes, such as refrigeration, transportation of frozen goods, and in the entertainment industry for creating smoke or fog effects.**
 
• **It sublimes at 194.7 K (−78.5 °C; −109.2 °F) at Earth's atmospheric pressure.** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**
 
• Heavy water, or deuterium oxide, is a form of water in which the hydrogen atoms are replaced by deuterium, a heavier isotope of hydrogen.
 
 
• **It is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.**
 
 
 
• Aspirin, also known as acetylsalicylic acid, is a medication used for pain relief, fever reduction, and anti-inflammatory purposes.
 
• Table sugar, or sucrose, is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.
 
 
• **It is commonly used as a sweetener in food and beverages.**

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the new Chief of Defence Staff in September 2022?

__
 
• Anil Chauhan:

 
 
• Born on May 18, 1961, General Anil Chauhan holds four stars in the Indian Army.
 
• Currently serving as the Indian Armed Forces' second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) since September 30, 2022.
 
• The Narendra Modi-led government recalled Chauhan from retirement on September 28, 2022, and named him as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS). This came about as a result of a June 2022 announcement that allowed military retirees under the age of 62 to be eligible for the position.
 
• **He** **became the** first three-star retiree to be appointed to the position, **which is** usually held by a four-star officer,** and took over as commander two days later.**
 
• General Bipin Rawat was the first person to hold the position, and he succeeded him.
 
• Awards:
 
 
• Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM)
 
• Uttam Yudh Seva Medal (UYSM)
 
• Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM)
 
• Sena Medal (SM)
 
• Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM)
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ajai Singh:

 
 
• He is a Retired Indian Army Lieutenant General.
 
• **He headed** Andaman and Nicobar Command (CINCAN) as its 16th Commander-in-Chief. **On June 1, 2021,** **he** succeeded Lieutenant-General Manoj Pande, PVSM, AVSM, VSM, in leadership.
 
• He was awarded: 
 
 
• Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM)
 
• Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM)
 
• Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM)
 
 
 
 
 
• Bipin Rawat:
 
 
• Four-star general of the Indian Army **General Bipin Rawat was an Indian military officer who served** from 16 March 1958 to 8 December 2021. **Before his death in a helicopter crash in December 2021, he was the** first Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of the Indian Armed Forces,** having taken** office in January 2020. **He held the positions of** 26th Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) and 57th Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (Chairman COSC) **of the Indian Armed Forces before becoming the CDS.**
 
• Awards:
 
 
• Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM)
 
• Uttam Yudh Seva Medal (UYSM)
 
• Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM)
 
• Sena Medal (SM)
 
• Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM)
 
 
 
 
 
• Manoj Pande:
 
 
• **Born on May 6, 1962, General Manoj Pande is a serving** four-star officer in the Indian Army.
 
• **He is** currently the 29th Chief of Staff.
 
• **He had held the positions of** Vice Chief of Staff, Eastern Command's General Officer-Commanding-in-Chief, and Andman and Nicobar Command's Commander-in-Chief (CINCAN)** in the past.**
 
• He is the first officer to hold the position of Army Chief from both the Corps of Engineers and non-infantry/armoured corps.
 
• He was awarded: 
 
 
• Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM)
 
• Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM)

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the fundamental duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Part IV A** ****of the Indian Constitution contains** Article 51A, **which deals with the** Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Soviet Constitution (USSR) **is where the** idea of fundamental duties originated.
 
• **Fundamental Duties were** recommended** in** 1976** by** the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• Fundamental duties are not subject to legal action unless specifically stated in a provision, in contrast to fundamental rights, which are justiciable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added ten fundamental duties.
 
• The 86th Amendment** to the Constitution was passed** **in** 2002, adding the eleventh fundamental duty.
 
• The list of Fundamental Duties as mentioned in the Article 51A:

 
 

 
 
S.No.

 
 
 
Fundamental Duties

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 
 
Abide by the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

 
 
 

 
 
2.

 
 
 
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom

 
 
 

 
 
3.

 
 
 
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

 
 
 

 
 
4.

 
 
 
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so

 
 
 

 
 
5.

 
 
 
Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

 
 
 

 
 
6.

 
 
 
Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture

 
 
 

 
 
7.

 
 
 
Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures

 
 
 

 
 
8.

 
 
 
Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

 
 
 

 
 
9.

 
 
 
Safeguard public property and to abjure violence

 
 
 

 
 
10.

 
 
 
Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement

 
 
 

 
 
11.

 
 
 
Provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

questions.question:
Which of the following forms an asset for a bank?

I. Reserves

II. Loans
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An asset is something of value that can be owned by an individual or an organization and can be used to produce something profitable.
 
• For a bank, these are the resources that generate income and profit.
 
• A bank has assets such as cash held in its vaults and moneys that the bank holds at the Federal Reserve bank (called “reserves”), loans that are made to customers.
 
• Other assets for a bank can include investments, such as stocks and bonds, and physical assets, such as buildings and equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserves, which are the funds held by the bank to meet its obligations and cover any potential losses, are considered an asset for the bank.
 
 
• **This is because the reserves can be used to make loans or investments that generate income for the bank.**
 
• These are important for a bank because they act as a buffer against unexpected losses.
 
 
• **Banks are required by regulatory authorities (like the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in India) to hold a certain amount of reserves to ensure financial stability. e.g., CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio).**
 
 
 
 
 
• Loans are also considered an asset for the bank.
 
 
• When a bank makes a loan, it expects to receive interest payments from the borrower over time. This interest income is a source of revenue for the bank and is considered an asset.
 
 
 
• **Reserves are typically low-risk and low-return, while loans are higher-risk and higher-return.**

questions.question: Where was the Communist Party of India (CPI) founded, in 1920?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tashkent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Communist Party of India (CPI):

 
 
• It is a left-wing political party in India, founded in 1920 in Tashkent (now the capital of Uzbekistan).
 
• M.N. Roy was the first elected Commintern leader.
 
• **The CPI was** formally founded in 1925** at the Indian Communist Conference in **Kanpur.
 
• It declared that revolution would be used to build socialism in India.
 
• Among its founders were M. N. Roy, his wife Evelyn Trent, M. P. T. Acharya and Abani Mukherji.
 
• The CPI's first general secretary was S.V. Ghate.
 
• **Ideological differences led to the** split in the party in 1964 **when two different party conferences were held, one of CPI and one of the **Communist Party of India (Marxist).
 
• The Left Front governed West Bengal for 34 years (1977–2011) and Tripura for 25 years (1993–2018)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current scenario of CPI:**

 
 
• **The** **Election Commission of India recognized the CPI as a "National Party,"** **but** **on April 10, 2023, the commission revoked that recognition** **due to the party's persistently dismal election results.**
 
• The CPI was the only national political party in India to run under the same electoral emblem in every general election up until 2022.
 
• The **Communist Party of India held its 24th Party Congress at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, from October 14–18, 2022.**

questions.question: Which among the following folk dances is popularly known as the 'stick dance'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kolannalu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kolannalu:**

 
 
• **India is home to a number of popular folk dances, including the well-known Kolannalu stick dance from Andhra Pradesh. **
 
• The narrative of the wicked spirit Basavasura that transformed into deity assisting others is explained by the song, dance moves, and background music.
 
• The Kolannalu traditional dance is sometimes referred to as kolkolannalu and is widely known among the Andhra Pradeshi people as Kolattam in Telugu.
 
• It is also known as the "stick dance" because the performers use long sticks (called kolatams) as props during the dance.
 
• Kolattam is a traditional dance in which eight to forty ladies take part. The dancers follow the direction of a leader who forms two circles.
 
• **The dance is performed by the inner circle dancers striking on stickers while the outside circle dances around the sticks.**
 
• **Other Folk Dance of Andhra Pradesh:**
 
 
• Bhagotam
 
• Burrakatha
 
• Kuchipudi
 
• Bhamakalapam
 
• Butta Bommalu
 
• Dappu
 
• Perini
 
• Tappeta Gullu
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghodemodni:**

 
 
• **An essential type of warrior folk dance, ghodemodni is performed in Bicholim (Goa) during Shigmo.**
 
• It is a reflection of the rich fighting heritage that the Maratha community, who came from the Ghat region, inherited. 
 
• Every member of the Ravalnathkar, Madwal, Saterkar, and Mahamayakar groups participates in this folk dance during Ghodemodni, dressing as a horse and donning white garments. 
 
• It is performed by men and women, and involves intricate footwork and rhythmic movements.
 
 
 
• **Theyyam:**
 
 
• Theyyam is one of the several dance styles that Kerla is famous for.
 
• **The word for God in Malayalam, daivam, is the source of theyyam.**
 
• Despite being a dance style, it is not performed for amusement.
 
• This is a ceremonial performance of centuries-old worship—a dance of the gods.
 
• This dancing worship, which is primarily practiced in Kerala's northern regions, aims to bring divine and mankind together.
 
• Prior to calling upon the deity, the (mostly) male dancer gets dolled up in cosmetics and clothing.
 
• Then he looks into his own reflection in a tiny mirror he's holding in his palm. We refer to this action as mukha darshan.
 
 
 
• **Koli:**
 
 
• **One of Maharashtra's most well-known dance styles, Koli gets its name from the Kolis, the state's fishermen.**
 
• Fishing and the sea, two activities that this community is most familiar with, are incorporated into the dance.
 
• Men and women separate into groups of two and perform this dance style.
 
• These fisherman use this dancing form to depict the motion of rowing a boat. In addition, the dancers simulate the motion of the waves and the launching of nets to capture fish.
 
• The women who work as fishers are positioned in the opposing rows, reaching out towards men with linked arms.
 
 
 
• **Some more folk dances:**

 Dekhni, Dashavatara, Dhalo, Dhangar, Goff, Kunbi, Divlyan Nach, Veerbhadra, Romta Mel, Correndinho, Ghodemodni.

 **Kerla**
 Thirayattam, Padayani, Kali Kakrisi, Kuttiyottama, Kaikottikali

questions.question: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bilateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A bilateral trade agreement is a pact between two parties, countries, or regions that outlines the terms and conditions for trade between them.**

 
 
• In it, both parties agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to promote trade and investment.
 
• It can help to increase economic growth, create job opportunities, and improve the standard of living in both countries.
 
• **India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) are examples of bilateral agreements.**
 
 
 
• Trade Agreements** **are treaties in which a country promises to engage in fewer trade protections with another country (or countries) to engage in more trade.
 
 
• It can be between two countries or between many countries.
 
• Important terms of trade between them include tariffs, quotas, restrictions on imports and exports, and provisions such as trade facilitation, intellectual property rights, and investment protection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A multilateral trade agreement involves three or more countries or regions that agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers.
 
 
• **The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), among the 15 members, is an example.**
 
• **The World Trade Organization (WTO) is another example of a multilateral trade agreement.**
 
 
 
• A tripartite trade agreement involves three parties, usually countries or regions, that agree to promote trade and investment between them.
 
 
• The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is an example of a tripartite trade agreement between the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
 
 
 
• **A unilateral trade agreement is a decision made by one country or region to reduce or eliminate trade barriers without the agreement of another party.**
 
 
• This is usually a preferential arrangement that a developed country makes for imports from developing countries.
 
• The United States has unilateral trade policies under the Generalized System of Preferences.

questions.question: Who took over as the Chief Executive Officer of National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog in July 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parameswaran Iyer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parameswaran Iyer:**

 
 
• **Born on April 16, 1959, Parameswaran Iyer is an Indian government servant who served as NITI Aayog's CEO from July 1, 2022, to February 28, 2023.**
 
• He was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog in July 2022, succeeding Amitabh Kant.
 
• In 1981, he enlisted in the Indian Civil Services. He voluntarily retired in 2009 to take a position managing the World Bank's water resources.
 
• He joined the Indian government's Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation in 2016, and Prime Minister Modi designated him to lead the Swachh Bharat Mission's initiatives for water management and sanitation.
 
• **He is presently the India's nominee as an executive director in World Bank.**
 
 
 
• NITI Aayog:
 
 
• The Government of India's premier think tank on public policy, NITI Aayog is the nodal agency responsible for promoting cooperative federalism, encouraging economic development, and eschewing bargaining federalism by involving State Governments of India in the formulation of economic policies through a bottom-up methodology. 
 
• **It took over the role of the Planning Commission when it was founded in 2015.**
 
• Chairperson: Narendra Modi, The Prime Minister (ex-officio)
 
• Vice Chairperson: Suman Bery
 
• CEO: B. V. R. Subrahmanyam
 
• HQ: New Delhi, India
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narendra Singh Tomar:**

 
 
• Narendra Singh Tomar is an Indian politician.
 
• He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• **At present, he serves as the fifteenth Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• Additionally, he served as a member of Fifteenth Lok Sabha from Morena (2009 - 2014), the Sixteenth Lok Sabha from Gwalior from 2014 to 2019, and the Seventeenth Lok Sabha from Morena from 2019 to 2023.
 
• **Arvind Virmani:**
 
 
• Arvind Virmani, an Indian economist, was born on June 22, 1949.
 
• **He is a full-time member of NITI Aayog since November 2022.**
 
• In 2009, he was designated as the representative of India at the International Monetary Fund.
 
• As the 13th Government of India's Chief Economic Advisor from 2007 to 2009, Virmani authored the 2008–2009 Economic Survey of India.
 
• He is the creator of the non-profit, multidisciplinary EGROW Foundation, which conducts independent, first-rate research in the fields of national security, public welfare, macroeconomic policy, and diplomacy.

questions.question: ___________ are promoted throughout the country to save energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light Emitting Diode Lamps.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LED Lamps:**

 
 
• It stands for** ****Light Emitting Diode** Lamps. 
 
• **Compared to incandescent light bulbs, LED lighting products provide light up to 90% more effectively. **
 
• Visible light is produced when an electrical current flows through a microchip, illuminating the small light sources known as LEDs. 
 
• Heat sinks are used by LEDs to absorb their own heat and release it into the surrounding air. This prevents LEDs from burning out or overheating.
 
• Compared to both incandescent and fluorescent lights, the lifespan of commercial LED lamps is far longer.
 
• **Unlike incandescent and CFL light sources, which release light and heat in all directions, LED light sources are "directional," meaning they focus their light emission in a single direction.**
 
• This implies that LEDs can use light and energy more effectively in a variety of applications.
 
• All LED products that have been awarded the ENERGY STAR have undergone testing to guarantee that, regardless of the heat sink design, they effectively manage heat to maintain light output until the end of their rated life.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Compact Fluorescent Lamps:**

 
 
• Compact fluorescent lamps are energy-efficient bulbs that use up to 75% less energy than traditional incandescent bulbs and last up to 10 times longer.
 
• They are widely promoted as an eco-friendly lighting option.
 
• An electric current travels between electrodes at either end of a gas-filled tube in a CFL.
 
• Heat and ultraviolet (UV) light are produced by this process.
 
• When the UV light hits the phosphor coating inside the lightbulb, it is converted to visible light. 
 
 
 
• **Incandescent bulb:**
 
 
• **Incandescent bulbs are the traditional, inefficient lighting option that has been phased out in many countries due to their high energy consumption and short lifespan.**
 
• A metal filament within an incandescent lightbulb is heated by electricity to a "white" temperature, a process known as incandesce.
 
• Consequently, 90% of the energy in incandescent bulbs is released as heat.
 
• They are not typically promoted as an energy-saving option.
 
 
 
• **Oil lamps**:
 
 
• **Oil lamps are not an energy-efficient option.**
 
• They use Hydrocarbon as fuel.
 
• Typically used for decorative or emergency purposes rather than everyday lighting.

questions.question: The Consumer Protection Act provides for a ___________ tier Consumer Disputes Redressal Agencies in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Consumer Protection Act, 1986**:

 
 
• The historic Consumer Protection Act, passed by the Indian Parliament in 1986, is a significant piece of socio-economic law that aims to promote public welfare by allowing consumers to engage directly in the market.
 
• The Act's goal when it was passed was to give greater protection to consumer interests. Its purpose was to protect customers from unfair business practices and other forms of abuse by offering them effective and efficient safeguards.
 
• It **encompasses all industries viz. public, commercial, and cooperative—and all goods and services**.
 
• **The following rights were enshrined in the Act:**
 
 
• Right to Safety
 
• Right to be informed
 
• Right to Choose
 
• Right to be Heard
 
• Right to seek Redressal
 
• Right to Consumer Education
 
 
 
• **Three-tiered Consumer Disputes Redressal agencies are established in India under the Consumer Protection Act. They are as follows:**
 
 
• **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** (value of goods or services involved is up to Rs. 20 lakhs)
 
• **State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission **(value of goods or services involved is between Rs. 20 lakhs and Rs. 1 crore)
 
• **National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** (value of goods or services involved is over Rs. 1 crore)
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On August 6, 2019, the Parliament passed the historic Consumer Protection Bill, 2019 with the goal of addressing the new issues that customers face in the digital age and offering prompt and efficient administration and resolution of consumer complaints.
 
• The President of India has signed the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
 
• **Salient feature of Consumer Protection Act, 2019**:
 
 
• Inclusion of e-commerce, since e-commerce transactions were not expressly covered by the previous Act.
 
• Section 2(7) defines "consumer" more broadly, encompassing both offline and online transactions.
 
• The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) will be established under the New Act in order to regulate matters pertaining to consumer rights violations, unfair trade practices, and deceptive or false advertisements that harm the interests of the public and consumers. Additionally, the CCPA will be responsible for promoting, safeguarding, and enforcing the rights of consumers as a class.
 
• Filing of complaints electronically online.
 
• The New Act streamlines and expedites the dispute adjudication process by offering mediation as an Alternate Dispute Resolution tool.
 
• **Enhanced three-tiered Consumer Disputes Redressal agencies are established in India under the Consumer Protection Act. They are as follows:**
 
 
• District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (value of goods or services involved is up to Rs. 1 crore)
 
• State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (value of goods or services involved is between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 10 crore)
 
• National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (value of goods or services involved is over Rs. 10 crore)

questions.question: Agriculture and fishing activities belong to which sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary sector.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Products and services are produced as a result of economic activity, and sectors are collections of economic activities categorised according to certain standards.
 
• Based on ownership, labour conditions, and the type of activity, the Indian economy can be divided into several sectors.
 
• **Economic sector types according to the type of activity:**
 
 
• **Primary Sector**
 
• **Secondary Sector**
 
• **Tertiary Sector**
 
• **Quaternary Sector**
 
 
 
• **Primary Sector**:
 
 
• Activities in the primary sector of the economy involve the direct use of natural resources.
 
• Some examples of this industry are agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry, dairy, and so on.
 
• It is thus named because it serves as the foundation for all other goods.
 
• It is also known as the "agriculture and allied sector" because the majority of the natural products we use come from forestry, fishery, dairy, and agriculture.
 
• Because primary activities require working outside, those who engage in them are referred to as red-collar workers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secondary Sector:**

 
 
• It encompasses the sectors in which natural resources generated in the primary sector are used to create final goods.
 
• This sector includes operations such as sugar cane production, cotton fabric production, and industrial production.
 
• Therefore, manufacturing is the sector of a nation's economy that produces goods as opposed to raw materials.
 
• This sector is also known as the industrial sector because it is connected to several industries.
 
• Blue collar workers are those who perform auxiliary tasks. 
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• The primary and secondary sectors benefit from the activity of this sector.
 
• Economic activity in the tertiary sector assists or supports production rather than producing commodities on its own.
 
• It is also known as Service Sector.
 
• The industry includes things like banking, insurance, finance, and truck or train-borne freight.
 
• It adds value to a product in the same way as the secondary sector.
 
• White collar jobs are those in this industry.
 
 
 
• **Economic sector types depending on labour conditions:**
 
 
• **Organised Sector**
 
• **Unorganised Sector**
 
 
 
• **Organised Sector:**
 
 
• Employees in this industry are guaranteed employment and social security, and job terms are regular and set.
 
• It may also be described as an industry that is registered with the government and to which certain acts are applicable to the businesses.
 
• The organized sector includes hospitals and schools.
 
• Employees in the organized industry are guaranteed a job. They have a set amount of hours that they are required to work. The company must give them extra pay if they put in more hours.
